A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 15-page versions of MetricHMSR, including the four-page supplementary material in Sections 6–7. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support a reliable comparison of all scientific content.

before.justification: v3 reports original human mesh, trajectory, and depth reconstruction experiments in Tables 1–6, with additional robustness and shape results in supplementary Tables 7–8.

after.justification: v4 retains the same original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, and supplementary robustness and shape evaluations.

M1.justification: The bounding ray representation, Patch and Global HumanMoE components, human-guided depth refinement, and training objectives are identical in Sections 3 and 6.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is unchanged, including BEDLAM, AIC, COCO, MPII, 3DPW, EMDB, RICH, PROX, and SynFocal. No task, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in every corresponding experiment. This includes Metric3D, Unidepth, and MapAnything in Table 5; Human3R in supplementary Table 7; and PromptHMR in Table 8.

E3.justification: Training budgets, preprocessing, metrics, and evaluation settings are unchanged, including 40-epoch MetricHMR training, predicted versus ground-truth extrinsic evaluations, and the PROX 9:1 train/test split.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical component and expert-count ablations in Table 6, routing analyses in Figures 5 and 11–12, focal-length and bounding-box robustness analyses, and supplementary trajectory comparisons.

E5.justification: No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-test reporting is added or revised. Existing root-position dispersion and shape-variance reporting in supplementary Tables 7–8 is identical.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 4 retains 3DPW PA-MPJPE/MPJPE/PVE of 33.6/53.0/62.7, and Table 5 retains PROX AbsRel/MAE/delta1 of 0.13/0.46/0.91 for the proposed method. Supplementary results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, camera geometry, MoE and loss formulations, and supplementary mathematical definitions are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims concerning metric human–scene reconstruction, feature disentanglement, depth refinement, and pseudo-ground-truth generation.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are identical. Both retain the limitations concerning multi-person interaction and severe occlusion, and the supplementary explanation for using predicted depth as initialization rather than a human-pose constraint.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, data-processing instructions, and supplementary architecture descriptions are unchanged. The project-page address and its hyperlink target are also identical.

R1.justification: The same 65 references and research-positioning discussions appear in both versions, including the supplementary discussion of BEDLAM2.0 relative to SynFocal.

P1.justification: The acknowledgments replace NSFC grant No.62171255 with No.62422110 on PDF page 8. The margin stamp changes from v3 dated 31 March 2026 to v4 dated 30 June 2026. All other wording and document organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All 16 figures, eight tables, captions, and main-text and supplementary layouts are unchanged. The updated margin stamp introduces no figure, table, or structural layout revision.

improvement.justification: The only changes are the funding grant identifier and arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and visual presentation remain unchanged throughout the main paper and supplement, establishing no meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
